title: Drop Goes Looking for the Sea
summary: A little raindrop dreams of being as big as the sea, and jumps out of her cloud on a journey to reach it.

scenes.text:
High up in the sky, inside a cloud as soft as cotton wool, lived a very small drop of water. Her name was Drop.

From up there, every day, she looked at the sea.

It was enormous. Blue. Shining. It went on as far as your eyes could see.

"I want to be like that," Drop sighed. "Big, really big. Like the sea."

One morning, the cloud turned grey and plump. Drop felt a tickle, like when you're just about to slip.

And then the cloud began to rain.

"Here I gooo!" shouted Drop.

She fell, spinning round and round, like on a slide with no slide, along with thousands and thousands of other drops. The air tickled her. For a moment, she forgot to be scared.

Below, a green mountain was waiting for her with open arms.

Drop landed on a leaf. Plip!

She slid down the leaf to the very tip, hung there for a second… and dropped into the water of a stream.

The water raced down the mountain, leaping between the stones.

Drop was tossed this way and that, dizzy and happy. She went under a log bridge. She tumbled down a teeny waterfall, wheee!, and landed in a pool full of foam.

Little by little, the water became a river. Wide, slow and calm.

And there were more and more drops. They came from the clouds, from the snow on the mountains, from other faraway rivers.

Drop began to worry.

"There are so many of us," she thought. "If I join all of them, won't I get lost? Won't I stop being me?"

Floating beside her was a very old drop, who had come from a glacier.

"You never stop being you," she said. "You just stop being alone."

And then, round a bend, the river opened out.

And there it was.

The sea.

Enormous, blue, shining, so big you couldn't take it in with one look. A wave lifted Drop into the air and let her fall among the foam and the bubbles.

"I'm here!" she shouted. "I'm the sea!"

Drop looked around. Millions of drops just like her were rocking together, rising and falling, all at the same time.

And she understood.

She wasn't the sea on her own. She was the sea together with all the others. And that was much, much lovelier.

That afternoon, the sun warmed the water gently, golden and soft.

Drop felt light. As light as a sigh.

And without stopping being herself, she began to rise. She floated up through the air, back to the sky, into a new cloud as soft as cotton wool.

From up there she looked down at the sea, glittering in the sunset.

"I was the sea," she said softly, and smiled.

She snuggled into her cloud, warm and calm.

Tomorrow she'll fall again. Maybe on a garden. Maybe on a river. Maybe on your window.
